subject: Hosted-to-Dedicated sizing validation & cutover timeline — BioMend
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Thomas <sarah.thomas@biomend.com>, BioMend Procurement <procurement@biomend.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-15T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted-to-Dedicated sizing validation & cutover timeline — BioMend

Hi Sarah / BioMend procurement team,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. I attached a first-pass rightsize workbook (BMT_rightsize_calc.xlsx) — high level assumptions are included on the cover tab. Before we lock a Dedicated commit and propose cutover dates I need confirmation on three things from your side: 

- Peak traffic pattern (spikes per minute and typical sustained QPS over 10-minute windows). Our worksheet currently uses a conservative 220 req/s peak with 12k tokens average per request.
- Latency SLAs you need at P95/P99 (we've assumed P99 < 800ms for the scoring route).
- Preferred maintenance time windows for the canary & final cutover (we typically ask for an evening UTC-8 2–4 hour window).

Assumptions baked into the calc: 1) GPUs: two production H100-80GB instances (cluster of 4 cards via multi-instance) + one A100-80GB canary pool; 2) KV cache warm rates of ~60% after 10 min (we see ~20–30% cost reduction in practice); 3) batching target of 4–8 tokens for average chat flows.

Proposed validation sequence (high level):
1) Sizing validation: run 72-hour soak on hosted replication with synthetic traffic that matches your 95th/99th patterns.
2) Cutover dry-run: smoke + rollback rehearsal (1–2 hours) in a reserved carve-out with mirrored traffic.
3) Canary: shift 5–10% traffic for 48 hours, monitor latency/cost/quality.
4) Full cutover: switch DNS + capacity commit with 48-72h watch window and defined rollback triggers.

If you can confirm the traffic and SLA pieces by EOD Mon (1/19) I’ll produce a detailed timeline and we can slot dry-run dates.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions — Redwood Inference
Attach: BMT_rightsize_calc.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)

From: Sarah Thomas <sarah.thomas@biomend.com>

Date: 2026-01-16T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted-to-Dedicated sizing validation & cutover timeline — BioMend

Thanks Karthik — quick answers below: 

- Typical peak: 200–240 req/s during clinical report generation bursts (peaks last ~10–15 minutes); sustained normal load ~60–80 req/s.
- Latency targets: P95 < 500ms, P99 < 900ms (our product team is strict on P95 for user-facing flows).
- Preferred windows: M–F 02:00–05:00 UTC-8 for final cutover; can do dry-runs in the same window. Weekends are possible but procurement prefers weekday scheduling.

Procurement: we’ll need the SLA draft and committed capacity numbers for review. Also include a proposed migration credit/discount if we commit 12 months up front.

Sarah
Sarah Thomas
Head of Platform Engineering — BioMend Therapeutics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-18T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Hosted-to-Dedicated sizing validation & cutover timeline — proposed commit / GPU plan

Marissa / Lauren — forwarding Sarah's answers. Based on their confirmed peaks I updated the rightsize calc and sketched an internal recommendation: 

Proposal (preliminary):
- Production pool: 4x H100-80GB (split across 2 nodes for redundancy) — this covers peak bursts with horizontal headroom for batching inefficiencies.
- Canary pool: 1x A100-80GB equivalent (single node) for warm-up and traffic shadowing.
- Autoscale buffer: additional 20% headroom in reserved capacity for first 30 days as we tune batchers and cache TTLs.

Rationale: With KV-cache warm of ~60% we can trust the H100 set for the heavy tail while the A100 canary validates open-model quirks. The attached calc shows expected token costs and latency profiles for a 220 req/s synthetic run.

Ask: approve the proposal so I can convert to a pending Dedicated offer and include the SLA draft for procurement. Also note: BioMend has requested a 12‑month commit with a discount conversation — suggest we prepare a migration credit to mitigate cutover risk (15–20% one-time credit).

Karthik

Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted-to-Dedicated sizing validation & cutover timeline — proposed commit / GPU plan

Karthik / Marissa — good baseline. A couple of asks before we present to procurement: 

1) Acceptance SLOs — define concrete pass/fail triggers for the canary and full cutover (e.g., sustained P95 < 550ms for 1 hour AND error rate < 0.5%). Include alerting escalation and ownership.
2) Rollback window — we should make the rollback window explicit: 48 hours after cutover with a documented runbook and clear traffic switchback steps.
3) Cross-functional cutover call — include CS, Infra/NetOps, and Eng-on-call. Schedule 30–45m the week prior for runbook dry-run.

Approve proceeding to convert to an offer contingent on the items above. For the migration credit ask Marissa to draft a 12-month commitment term with a suggested 15% migration credit that procurement can accept into the DocuSign packet.

Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Sarah / Procurement — confirming the timeline and next steps so everyone has an actionable schedule: 

- Jan 20–Feb 09: sizing validation & soak on hosted replica (we’ll share a runbook and synthetic workload).
- Feb 10 (02:00–05:00 UTC-8): Dry-run smoke + rollback rehearsal in reserved carve-out.
- Feb 17–19: Canary window — shift 5–10% user traffic; monitor SLOs (P95/P99/err rate) and quality regressions.
- Feb 24 (02:00–05:00 UTC-8): Full cutover; 48h watch window, rollback triggers defined in runbook.

Attachments: SLA_DRAFT_Redwood.pdf (for procurement review). DocuSign packet will be ready once procurement confirms the 12-month commit level. HubSpot opportunity link included for cross-reference.

If these dates work I’ll schedule the cross-functional dry-run call for week of Feb 2 and circulate the runbook + acceptance checklists.

Best,
Karthik
